steps.name: Sample structure QC (batch vs condition)
steps.context: Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, two known batches balanced across condition, raw salmon counts. This QC step follows the DESeq2 blind-vst + PCA + sample-distance-heatmap procedure grounded by the knowledge service (R-0033).
steps.question: Do the 12 kidney samples separate by treated-vs-control or by the two processing batches on the top-variance genes, and are library sizes comparable across batch and condition?

grounding.reason: Known-balanced-batch design with raw counts: blind vst + PCA on top 500 genes + sample distance heatmap, colored by condition and batch, per R-0033.

steps.description: Load the raw count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples) and the metadata (condition, batch), build a DESeqDataSet with design ~batch+condition, apply a blind variance-stabilizing transform, run PCA on the top 500 most variable genes, and draw a sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap. Color/label all plots by both condition and batch to check whether the balanced-batch design behaves as expected (no gross batch-driven separation dominating over condition) and to flag any outlier sample.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot colored by condition and by batch is produced
Sample distance heatmap is produced
Library size per sample is reported
Any sample departing from its group is flagged with a stated reason

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression (treated vs control, batch-adjusted)
steps.context: 12000 x 12 raw integer salmon counts, metadata has condition and batch columns; batch is a known covariate balanced across condition (6/6 in each), so it enters the model as a fixed design term per the knowledge-service rule for known_balanced batch structure (R-0006, R-0012). Replicate count (n=6/6) falls in the DESeq2 Wald + apeglm regime (R-0001, R-0009).
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples, after accounting for the two known processing batches?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with design ~batch+condition, apeglm shrinkage, BH/independent filtering at alpha 0.05, per the full-plan procedure returned for this exact situation (known_balanced batch, n=6/6, salmon counts, human).

steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~batch+condition, setting control as the reference level of condition explicitly. Run DESeq() with the Wald test; do not pre-normalize or batch-correct the counts, since DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors and the batch design term handle this internally. Extract results() for the contrast condition treated vs control at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering on, then apply apeglm shrinkage (lfcShrink, coef = condition_treated_vs_control) for the reported/ranked log2 fold change. Report both the unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE. Inspect and report the raw p-value histogram shape. Report counts flagged as outliers (Cook's distance, NA p-values) separately from genes removed by independent filtering. Save the full and significant (padj<0.05) results tables.
acceptance_criteria: Design formula ~batch+condition is used with condition reference level stated explicitly
Pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=6 samples applied before the test
Results table reports unshrunken log2FC, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per gene
Number of genes tested after filtering and number of genes with padj<0.05 are reported
MA plot and dispersion plot are produced as fit diagnostics
p-value histogram is produced and its shape is reported
Genes with NA p-values from Cook's-distance outlier flagging are reported separately from independent-filtering NAs

steps.name: Over-representation analysis of significant DE genes (Hallmark + Reactome)
steps.context: The knowledge-service enrichment-check for this exact situation (n=6/6, known_balanced batch, human) rejected preranked GSEA and approved only over-representation analysis with an explicit universe as the permitted enrichment method, so ORA against Hallmark and Reactome gene sets is used instead of fgsea. Human Hallmark (50 sets) and Reactome pathway gene sets are staged in the reference store; if either is unavailable at run time, the step should report that collection as skipped rather than fail.
steps.question: Which Hallmark and Reactome gene sets are over-represented among the genes significantly different between treated and control kidney samples?

grounding.reason: knowledge_check rejected fgsea preranked GSEA for this situation (rule R-0048) and permitted only over-representation analysis with an explicit universe; step revised to ORA on the significant gene list against Hallmark then Reactome, universe = tested genes.

steps.description: Map the tested-gene symbols and the significant (padj<0.05) gene symbols to Entrez IDs using org.Hs.eg.db, reporting the unmapped share. Using clusterProfiler::enricher (or equivalent hypergeometric ORA), test the significant gene list against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets and, as a second pass, the Reactome human gene sets, with the universe set explicitly to the full list of genes that passed the DE pre-filter (tested genes), not the whole genome. Restrict gene sets to those with 15-500 members after intersecting with the universe. Apply BH correction to the ORA p-values. Before running, report the number of significant genes found in T1S2; if fewer than ~50, state explicitly in the output that the ORA result has limited power at that list size (per the knowledge-service warning) and interpret findings cautiously.
acceptance_criteria: Universe is explicitly set to the tested-gene list from T1S2, not the whole genome
Gene sets outside the 15-500 member window (after universe intersection) are excluded
Both Hallmark and Reactome ORA results are reported with BH-adjusted p-values
The number of significant input genes is stated, with a low-power caveat if under ~50
Unmapped symbol-to-Entrez share is reported

steps.context: Final synthesis step drawing on T1S2 (DE results) and T2S1 (enrichment results) for the kidney treated-vs-control comparison.
steps.question: What is the final set of genes differing between treated and control kidney samples, with what confidence, and what functional themes do they implicate?

grounding.reason: No single rule covers the composite report step; it aggregates the reporting-content rules (versions, thresholds, diagnostics, reproducibility record) that the knowledge service returned as separate report-step guidance.

steps.description: Assemble a report combining: the design (design formula ~batch+condition, reference level, contrast name), package versions and session info, the QC PCA/heatmap, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes at padj<0.05, the MA and dispersion diagnostic plots, the p-value histogram and its shape, the top DE genes ranked by shrunken log2FC with unshrunken log2FC/lfcSE/padj alongside, the ORA results for Hallmark and Reactome with the universe and size-window stated, and a stated caveat that the enrichment reflects one method (ORA) chosen because the DE gene list did not support a preranked test per the project's method-selection rule. Include the full reproducibility record (sessionInfo, package versions, gene-set collection versions/dates).
acceptance_criteria: Report states design formula, reference level, contrast, alpha, and package versions
Report states number of genes tested and number of DE genes at padj<0.05
Report includes MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram
Report lists top DE genes with both shrunken and unshrunken log2FC, lfcSE, and padj
Report includes ORA results for Hallmark and Reactome with stated universe and gene-set size window
Report includes a full reproducibility record (session info, seed if applicable, package and reference versions)

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch covariate
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve kidney samples (6 treated, 6 control) were processed in two known batches, each batch balanced across conditions. Salmon-derived raw gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples after excluding the gene symbol column) are analyzed with DESeq2 using a design of ~batch + condition, so the batch is modeled as a fixed covariate rather than removed from the counts, preserving valid variance estimation per the knowledge-service recommendation for a known-balanced batch. QC first checks whether batch or condition dominates the sample structure. The Wald test on the condition coefficient, apeglm-shrunk fold changes, and BH-adjusted independent filtering yield the DE gene list. Because the knowledge-service enrichment-check rejected preranked fgsea for this situation and only approved over-representation analysis with an explicit universe, functional interpretation uses ORA (clusterProfiler) against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets, restricted to the tested-gene universe, gated on there being enough significant genes to give the test power. A final report consolidates diagnostics, gene tables, and enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata.
